findings.title: R6 gate metrics are hardcoded placeholders
findings.why_it_matters: The R6 gate contract presents these as operational guardrail metrics, but this implementation hardcodes them (0/0/true). That creates abstraction debt where future maintainers may assume real telemetry is wired while release decisions are effectively blind to stale-cache, graph-fallback, and security-check regressions.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace placeholder values with real counters sourced from cache read telemetry, graph-lane fallback telemetry, and an explicit security report signal. If telemetry is not ready, mark those metrics unavailable/insufficient and block gate pass per contract until wired.
evidence: apps/backend/src/modules/rag/quality/rag-quality.service.ts:701-727 sets staleCacheReadRate=0, graphFallbackActivationRate=0, securityGatePass=true in metricValues.
Repo search only finds these metric names in this service and assertions, with no producer telemetry paths.
docs/standards/r6-scale-gate-spec.md:32-35 defines these as live quantitative gate metrics, not defaults/placeholders.
Fresh verification: backend integration test `test/integration/r6-gate-readiness.spec.ts` passed while only validating decision outputs, not proving these three metrics come from real telemetry.

findings.title: Queue P95 uses wrong sample window count
findings.why_it_matters: The metric value is computed from a 6h slice, but sample count is taken from a 24h slice. This coupling mismatch can incorrectly satisfy or fail min-sample gates, making release decisions harder to reason about and less trustworthy.
findings.suggested_fix: Split datasource orchestration report counters by window (for example queueWaitSampleSize6h and isolationSampleSize24h) and use the window-matching sample count for each metric in snapshotR6; add tests with divergent 6h vs 24h sample volumes.
evidence: apps/backend/src/modules/rag/quality/rag-quality.service.ts:599-613 computes orchestratorQueueWaitP95Ms from last 6h but exposes sampleSize24h.
apps/backend/src/modules/rag/quality/rag-quality.service.ts:680-684 assigns orchestratorQueueWaitP95Ms metric samples from datasourceSamples (24h count).

findings.title: Graph lane scoring duplicated across fallback paths
findings.why_it_matters: Two near-identical scoring implementations exist for graph retrieval (fallback heuristic and acceleration path) with different constants. This raises coupling and drift risk: behavior can diverge depending on whether acceleration/breaker fallback is active, making tuning and incident analysis harder.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a shared graph-scoring strategy (single constants + scoring function) used by both RagRetrievalService fallback and GraphAccelerationAdapter, then add a parity test that verifies consistent ordering for identical inputs.
evidence: apps/backend/src/modules/rag/retrieval/rag-retrieval.service.ts:445-499 defines heuristic scoring for graph lane fallback.
apps/backend/src/modules/graph/adapter/graph-acceleration.adapter.ts:37-109 defines a second, very similar scoring pipeline with different weights.
apps/backend/src/modules/graph/graph.service.ts:38-47 and 85-105 switches between accelerated and fallback paths at runtime.

Fresh verification: integration tests `graph-acceleration-fallback.spec.ts` and `graph-acceleration-circuit-breaker.spec.ts` passed, confirming both paths are actively exercised and therefore drift-sensitive.

findings.title: Delivery normalization logic duplicated across clients
findings.why_it_matters: Contract-compat normalization now exists in multiple frontend modules with overlapping snake_case/camelCase fallback rules. This duplicates operational contract knowledge and increases drift risk when evidence fields evolve, causing inconsistent UI behavior by entry point.
findings.suggested_fix: Move delivery/evidence normalization into a shared frontend codec (or shared-types helper) and import it from run-visibility-mapper and api-client; keep one compatibility matrix and one test suite.
evidence: apps/frontend/src/components/chat/run-visibility-mapper.ts:120-205 normalizes run delivery evidence with dual naming compatibility.
apps/frontend/src/lib/api-client.ts:109-209 introduces overlapping semantic evidence compatibility normalization for run payloads.
Both modules maintain separate readString/readNumber/shape-fallback helpers, requiring synchronized edits for contract evolution.

Fresh verification: targeted tests `tests/unit/run-visibility-mapper.spec.ts` and `tests/unit/chat-rag-sync-stream-consistency.spec.tsx` pass, but they validate behavior per entry point rather than cross-module normalization parity.

residual_risks: The R6 quality gate surface is broad and recently introduced; without unified metric provenance, future metric additions are likely to repeat placeholder/window-coupling debt.
Graph retrieval behavior remains sensitive to runtime mode transitions (accelerated vs fallback), so ranking drift risk persists until scoring logic is unified.
testing_gaps: No parity test validates that accelerated graph scoring and fallback graph scoring produce consistent ordering for the same retrieval inputs.
No test asserts that each R6 metric sample count matches the metric's declared time window (for example 6h queue-wait metric using 6h sample count).
No test guards against placeholder metric values being used for gate-critical metrics (staleCacheReadRate, graphFallbackActivationRate, securityGatePass).

Frontend command `pnpm --filter @text2sql/frontend run test -- --runInBand tests/unit/chat-rag-sync-stream-consistency.spec.tsx` executes the full suite and currently fails at `tests/unit/chat-panel.spec.tsx` (missing role/name `展开思考过程`), indicating suite-level instability outside the targeted visibility-mapper checks.
